title: Bosonic codes from compact phase spaces
abstract: We present the algebraic structure of bosonic quantum error-correcting codes on genus-two Riemann surfaces. We explicitly construct the code words as automorphic forms and analytically generate the full tower of code spaces at all weights. We prove a fundamental no-go theorem: for any genus greater than one, the stabilizer group is non-amenable, forcing a strictly positive spectral gap in the stabilizer Hamiltonian. Consequently, no normalizable quantum state can satisfy all stabilizer conditions. This sharply contrasts with standard Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) codes, where the amenability of the stabilizer group $\mathbb{Z}^2$ permits approximate code words with arbitrary precision.
comment: 7 pages, 3 figures + Supplemental Material (30 pages, 4 figures). Code, notebooks, and data at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20585488

bite.hook: Proves a fundamental no-go theorem showing stabilizer groups are non-amenable on genus-two Riemann surfaces.
tldr: Investigated the algebraic structure of bosonic quantum error-correcting codes on genus-two Riemann surfaces.
Constructed code words as automorphic forms and analytically generated the full tower of code spaces.
Proved a no-go theorem showing non-amenable stabilizer groups force a strictly positive spectral gap.
bite.whyItMatters: Quantum error correction is vital for building fault-tolerant quantum computers, and understanding topological limits points researchers toward safer architectures.
bite.eli5: Imagine trying to tile a curved, multi-holed donut surface perfectly with error-correcting rules without leaving gaps. This study proves mathematically that for higher-complexity surfaces, perfect error-correcting grids like the standard ones are fundamentally impossible.
